title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Pollard rho in GT on Frobenius classes

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT (BLS12-381 fixed-argument pairing inversion into G1, C = 20,000), compute g = e(P0, Q) with one reduced pairing, find x = log_g z by parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points on classes under the order-12 Frobenius action z -> z^p (class size 12, N' = (r-1)/12 + 1), and output P = [x]P0. A fixed budget of T = 1.05 k + 2^64 walk steps, k = sqrt(0.98859 N'), halts with success probability at least 0.39 (birthday bound 1 - exp(-k(k-1)/(2N')) with a 5% margin). Total work is at most 2^126.19 dense Fp12 multiplication equivalents, including the pairing, jump table, 1.40 units per step (one dense multiplication plus 8,000 charged instructions of key computation), distinguished-point handling, walk starts, cycle handling, scalar multiplication and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^92.5 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^50 units and is included in the total; nonuniform advice is 2^0 bytes. The attack is classical and relies on the stated heuristics: random-mapping behaviour of the class walk with s = 2^20 branches and no unresolved long fruitless cycles.

experiments.purpose: End-to-end check of the Frobenius-class walk with conjugated jump tables on a small prime-order group with an order-12 exponent automorphism. This does not establish production costs.
